citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
A 16-year-old, female, Bobcat, Annabelle, had several thick, large, hair mats covering the dorsal part of her back and
thick, stringy hair clumps along both sides of her abdomen. The larger mats were approximately 3 inches in diameter or
about the size of a fist. The attending veterinarian (AV) is aware that this bobcat has had prior issues with mats; however,
according to the AV there had not been notification about this animal’s current condition of a matted coat. Matted hair
coats left untreated may lead to underlying skin conditions/infections, other health issues or discomfort. At time of
inspection this animal did not appear to have any visible indications of irritation or discomfort and no visible skin issues.
A 7-year-old male Sika deer, Akino, had overgrown, elongated nails on its left rear foot, which were curving inward and
overlapping. According to the attending veterinarian, there had not been notification about this animal’s current condition
of overgrown nails. In 2021 this deer was diagnosed and treated by the AV for a fracture of the hock of its left rear limb.
Due to this previous injury the deer does not bear any weight on this leg and keeps it lifted several inches off the ground.
Although the deer does not bear any weight on this limb, overgrown nails may lead to injury if these nails potentially
become caught on objects within the enclosure or the fencing while moving or lying down.
Daily observation of all animals to assess their well-being, and direct and frequent communication with the attending
veterinarian is required so that timely and accurate information on problems of animal health and well-being is conveyed
to the attending veterinarian.
Correct by 11/06/2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:

Mailstop #3W11
